_extraction_flags.notes: 📚 REVIEW PAPER - O-ISAC Tutorial/Survey in IEEE IoT Magazine. Covers waveform design (PPM, LFM-CPM, DCO-OFDM), RF vs O-ISAC comparison, future trends. Second review in corpus after O_ISAC_006 (Fiber-ISAC focused).

reasoning_trace.step_0_visual_inspection: Fig.1: Generalized O-ISAC system structure (block diagram). Fig.2: Three advantages (rate, precision, interference). Fig.3: Waveform design (pulsed, constant-modulus, multi-carrier). Fig.4: BER/RMSE simulation. Fig.5: Future trends + DL.
reasoning_trace.step_1_concept_analysis: Survey covering: (1) O-ISAC system structure, (2) Advantages over RF-ISAC, (3) Waveform design taxonomy (PPM, LFM-CPM, DCO-OFDM), (4) Resource allocation, (5) Future trends (OPA, hybrid RF-Optical, DL). Table 1 compares WiFi/mmWave/O-ISAC.
reasoning_trace.step_2_benchmark_verification: Table 1: O-ISAC achieves Gbps data rate, <1 km comm/sensing distance, cm-level resolution. Numerical simulation: 1 GHz DCO-OFDM, 200m FSO, BER 10^-5 at 11 dB (4QAM), RMSE 5 cm.
reasoning_trace.step_3_strategic_critique: Contribution: First comprehensive O-ISAC tutorial covering waveform design taxonomy. Compares with RF-ISAC. Highlights OPA and DL integration. Gap: Theoretical/conceptual - no novel system demonstration.

bibliographic.title: Optical Integrated Sensing and Communication: Architectures, Potentials and Challenges
bibliographic.authors: Yunfeng Wen, Fang Yang, Jian Song, Zhu Han

application.scenario_description: Tutorial/survey covering O-ISAC architectures, waveform design, and future trends for 6G applications.

enabling_tech.ml_details: Discusses DL for waveform design, resource allocation, target recognition, semantic communication.

key_contribution.key_contribution: Comprehensive O-ISAC tutorial covering system structure, waveform design taxonomy (PPM, LFM-CPM, DCO-OFDM), RF vs O-ISAC comparison, and future trends.
key_contribution.gap_addressed: Lack of unified O-ISAC framework and waveform design guidelines in literature.

transmitter.notes: DCO-OFDM: 256 subcarriers × 3.9 MHz = ~1 GHz. 32 OFDM symbols per frame. 4QAM or 16QAM per subcarrier.

receiver.notes: IM/DD with DC bias optimization. Sensing processing gain 39.1 dB.

integration.notes: Same DCO-OFDM waveform for comm and sensing. Element-wise-division at sensing Rx.

waveform.notes: DCO-OFDM: comm data on subcarriers, sensing via channel estimation from known symbols.

channel_wireless.notes: 200 m FSO link. Attenuation: -2.2 dB (comm), -23.2 dB (sensing). Atmospheric turbulence channel model.

comm_metrics.notes: BER 10^-5 at SNR 11 dB (4QAM, b=3σ). 16QAM requires ~20 dB.

sensing_metrics.notes: RMSE ~5 cm at high SNR. Threshold effect: sharp transition to precision region.

tradeoff.notes: DC bias vs subcarrier power trade-off. Low DC bias favors sensing, high DC bias favors comm.
